_authoring_conventions.note: Same conventions as fixtures/cinderella — see fixtures/authoring-notes.md. This package is original, written for this repository; nothing in it is adapted from an existing work.
_authoring_conventions.entry_state_and_exit_state: { <entity_id>: { <column>: <value>, ... }, ... } — one object per touched entity, naming only the core columns this scene asserts.
_authoring_conventions.new_rows_in_exit_state: Reserved keys _new_relationships / _new_character_knowledge, using the same row shape as world_model_seed.
_authoring_conventions.why_this_fixture_exists: The shortest package in the repository: three scenes, so a whole live telling costs three writer requests. It is the one to reach for when the question is whether the loop works, not whether the prose is good.

characters.name: Maudlin
characters.goal: get through the clover flow without incident

bag.occupation: keeps eleven hives on the south face of Barrow Hill
bag.manner: brisk, a little deaf, treats being slain as an item on an agenda

bag.note: knighted eleven days ago; the lance is borrowed and he has told nobody that
bag.manner: unfailingly polite, which is the whole of his problem
runs meetings the way weather runs

bag.description: a duck pond, a notice-board, and every opinion in the village standing on it
steep, chalky, and smelling faintly of something sweet the higher you go
eleven white hives in a row on the south face, and a dragon-sized gap where a twelfth would go

bag.note: belongs to Sir Pellow's aunt, who wants it back by Thursday

bag.description: a bellows-and-canister rig the size of a butter churn, packed with dried clover
twenty pounds of the first clover honey of the year

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Commission the knight, give the village a real and petty grievance, and lay down the detail that will turn the whole thing around — as a passing complaint, not a clue.
required_beats: Alderwoman Brisk commissions Sir Pellow to deal with the dragon on Barrow Hill, in front of everybody, so that he cannot say no
Nan Tolly holds up six weeks of washing gone grey and says the smoke off that hill has ruined every wash day since the thaw
somebody in the crowd says the smoke does not even smell like smoke, it smells like clover, and is told to be quiet
Sir Pellow starts up the hill with a borrowed lance and no plan
scene_cards.tone: village-meeting comedy; everyone certain, nobody informed
invariants: nobody in the village has been up the hill to look
the clover remark is thrown away, not dwelt on

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Collide the two genres: the knight arrives to slay a dragon and finds a beekeeper mid-inspection who treats him as an interruption.
required_beats: Sir Pellow comes over the ridge with the lance up and finds Maudlin in a veil the size of a mainsail, halfway through an inspection
Maudlin asks him to either put the lance down or stand downwind of it, because the bees are having a difficult morning
she works while they talk, and he cannot find the moment to announce what he came for
she opens the clover crock and gives him a spoonful, and he forgets the moment entirely
scene_cards.tone: warm, absurd, and entirely sincere on both sides
invariants: Sir Pellow never actually says the word slay out loud
the lance ends the scene leaning against a hive

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Collect the clover plant: the ruinous smoke is the smoker, the grievance is a scheduling problem, and the settlement makes everyone slightly better off than the fight would have.

bag.terms: honey down the hill, wash days on the calendar

required_beats: Brisk and Nan Tolly come up the hill expecting a body and find the two of them sitting down
the smoke the village has been cursing turns out to be the smoker, clover-packed, and it only runs on inspection days
Maudlin agrees to work the north face and to send word down the hill before she lights it, so wash day can move
the crock goes down to the green and the village drinks to a slaying that did not happen
scene_cards.tone: resolution as negotiation; the comedy is that it was always this easy
invariants: nobody apologises in so many words
Sir Pellow returns the lance unbloodied and does not correct anyone's account of the day

voice_card.narrative_distance: close on Pellow, with a narrator who finds him funny and is fond of him anyway
voice_card.register: light, dry, faintly rural; treats the extraordinary as a matter of parish administration
voice_card.sentence_rhythm: loose and conversational, with a short flat sentence dropped in to land a joke
imagery_palette: borrowed armour that does not fit
voice_card.dialogue_density: high; the story is mostly people talking slightly past each other
voice_card.style_exemplar: The dragon had eleven hives, a bad ear, and no interest whatever in being the third item on the parish agenda.
